Scottsdale Party Bus Rental: Seats, Rates and Stops

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a Scottsdale party bus rental as a chauffeured vehicle booked by the hour against a published rate, minimum and seat count. The Party Bus (28 Pax) is the largest here: $250 an hour on a 4-hour minimum, so a night starts at $1,000 before 8% tax — roughly $36 a seat, 28 aboard. The Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) start at $700; the Pink Hummer Limo at $1,180. Below: every party unit compared, how an Old Town night runs, what is allowed aboard, and how the quote is built. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 20, 2026

Which party vehicles can a Scottsdale group actually book?

5 party units lead this page and 6 executive shuttles trail it as the guest vehicle. The Party Bus (28 Pax) is the largest, at 28 seats and $250 an hour; the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) opens the range at $700 for the published minimum. Read the table as two blocks, not one ranked list. The party units are built for a night out: lounge or perimeter seating, and floor space to stand on in the larger ones. The executive shuttles beneath them are forward-facing seating, and they belong here only for the half of a group that wants a quiet ride to the same address. Seats are published seated capacity — a limit, not a target. Starting total is the published hourly rate times the billable hours at that vehicle's minimum, the arithmetic the checkout runs. It is a floor rather than a package: a longer night bills more hours and tax sits on top. What does a Scottsdale party bus rental cost?

A party bus is priced by the hour against a published minimum, so the 28-seat Party Bus (28 Pax) starts at $1,000 — $250 an hour across its 4-hour minimum — before 8% tax. Split across a full bus that is about $36 a seat for the night. The same arithmetic runs for every unit. The Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and the Limo Party Sprinter (12-13 Pax) share a rate of $175, so both open at $700; the Ultra Luxury Party Sprinter opens at $1,000 and the Pink Hummer Limo at $1,180. Those are the current published hourly rates and minimums, and they are what the booking flow charges against. Hours past the minimum bill at the same rate, and an hourly charter buys time rather than stops — so added stops cost nothing. A point-to-point transfer is the other product, and it charges $50 for each stop beyond pickup and drop-off. That is why a night with three or four stops is booked hourly. Payment follows the published deposit policy: pay 50% today by card and the balance is charged to that saved card 48 hours before pickup. A buy-now-pay-later method cannot be charged again later, so a trip paid that way is paid in full today. Availability is specific to a date and a vehicle, so request a current quote with your date, hours and group size.

How does an Old Town Scottsdale party bus night run?

Three operational facts decide whether a party bus night starts cleanly: the pickup address, the stop list and the single phone number the chauffeur calls. The Party Bus (28 Pax) needs room to stand and turn, so the reservation asks for a street address with curb space rather than a driveway. The service page states the pickup rule plainly: "A party bus needs room to stand and turn, so give us a street address with curb space rather than a driveway or a parking structure, and one phone we call for the group. List every stop on the reservation up front — stops on an hourly charter cost nothing." The last clause is the one groups underuse. What costs a night is never the second or third stop; it is the stop nobody wrote down. On-board space is the other honest limit: "There is real floor space on board, but it is shared with the people standing on it. If the night starts or ends with everyone’s overnight bags, tell us and we confirm the fit in writing." A party bus floor looks enormous until the group is standing on it. What the chauffeur handles is what guests least often ask for. The house rules invite it directly — "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really." Route, temperature, volume and the wait between stops are the chauffeur's job. What no reservation overrides is a valet or fire lane: where a commercial vehicle may legally stop is decided by the property on the night.

Which occasions in Scottsdale book a party bus?

Five celebration routes on this site point at a party bus: bachelorette, bachelor, birthday, the school dances — homecoming and prom — and a plain Old Town nightlife run. Each has its own page, and each opens on the same 5 party units rather than on an executive vehicle. A bachelorette or bachelor party is usually the whole guest list rather than a table of ten, and that is what moves a group from a limo Sprinter to a bus. Both have their own service page, on the same hourly pricing and house rules, as does a birthday. Homecoming and prom are the same booking on a different calendar: an adult holds the reservation, the guardian contact goes on it, and the under-21 rule below is worth reading aloud beforehand. A nightlife run is the simplest shape of all — a pickup, a listed loop of stops, a ride home — and it is what every other occasion is built on. For a mixed group the guest-shuttle rows exist so the quieter half rides to the same address on the same reservation.

What is allowed on board a Scottsdale party bus?

One page of house rules governs every trip here, whatever the vehicle, and 3 of those rules carry a stated fee. Drinking is allowed for guests 21 and over and eating is not, while smoking or vaping of any kind carries a $1,500 fee that no party-bus booking waives. The rules are published as written rather than summarised. On drinking: "Passengers 21 and over bring their own alcohol, and we do not sell it. Arizona vehicle-for-hire open-container policy, A.R.S. § 4-251, allows it, and if anyone under 21 rides, no alcohol comes on that trip." On its limit: "No underage drinking. Anyone under 21 stays on soft drinks." And on food: "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop." Three rules carry a fee, and each says why. "No smoking or vaping of any kind. The smell does not leave, so this one carries a fee." ($1,500). "Keep the drinks in the cups. Minor spills are fine; a can or two on the floor counts as excessive and carries a cleaning fee." ($450). And the one nobody plans for: "If someone gets sick in the vehicle, we have to deep clean it, and that carries a cleaning fee. Pace yourselves." ($450). Condition is documented instead of argued about afterwards. "Before every trip your chauffeur takes a documented set of photos of the interior. They are for our internal records only." "You authorize us to charge the card on file for damage beyond normal use. We will never charge for damage without telling you first, with the photos, so there are no surprises."

Is the pink party bus in this fleet a real vehicle?

Yes, with one correction worth making: the pink unit is the Pink Hummer Limo, a stretch limousine seating 18, not a bus. It is $295 an hour on a 4-hour minimum, so it starts at $1,180 — about $66 a seat. People searching for a pink party bus in Scottsdale mean this vehicle, so it is worth stating what it is. A limousine on a Hummer chassis seats fewer than a coach-built bus and loads differently: guests step down into a lounge rather than up into a standing cabin. For 18 or fewer who want the arrival photo it is the unit; for floor space, the Party Bus (28 Pax) is. It is the first row of the table above because that is the order the celebration pool is published in — a decision, not an accident of price. Per seat at the minimum it reads $66 against $44 for the Limo Party Sprinter (16 Pax) and $36 for the Party Bus (28 Pax), so compare that column before deciding.

Where outside Scottsdale does a party bus pick up?

10 metro cities have a published service-area page, and a party bus reservation can start in any of them. Pickup is a street address, not a zone, so a 24-seat shuttle and a 28-seat bus are quoted the same way wherever the night begins. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. A night that starts in one city and ends in another is still one hourly charter: the clock runs from first pickup to last drop-off, and the drive between cities sits inside that window rather than on top of it. Group size, not geography, changes the vehicle. Past the 28 seats of the largest bookable party bus the service page names the alternatives: "Hourly charters start at four hours. The largest party bus bookable here seats 28; past that a group moves on the 29-passenger Executive Mini Coach, the 56-passenger motorcoach, or a coordinated multi-vehicle fleet on one reservation. Anything the online quote cannot price — an unusual route, a multi-vehicle movement, a vehicle we hold for request only — goes to the reservations desk and comes back as a written quote before any card is charged." Those coaches — $225 an hour and $325 an hour, the motorcoach on a 5-hour minimum rather than 4 — are guest transport, not the celebration vehicle.

Things to know

  • How much is a party bus rental in Scottsdale? — The published 28-passenger Party Bus starts at $250 per hour with a four-hour minimum. Date, route, parking, tolls, overtime, and requested extras can change the final written price.
  • How many people fit in the Scottsdale party buses? — The published seating capacity is up to 28 guests. Tell the reservation team about luggage, coolers, mobility needs, or bulky gear because these can change the appropriate vehicle.
  • Can I request the 28-passenger party bus? — Yes. The 28-passenger party bus is the listed option, and the assigned vehicle is confirmed in writing before the reservation is final.
  • Is the party-bus photo the exact bus I get? — The listing shows a representative party-bus photo. It is not a photo of the bus assigned to your trip. Ask the reservation team to confirm current photos, cabin details, and the assigned bus in writing before the reservation is final.
  • Is this a self-drive party bus rental? — No. Every party-bus request is for chauffeured transportation. The selected vehicle, requested hours, route, and applicable terms are reviewed before confirmation.
  • Does submitting the form reserve the bus? — No. The form sends a pending availability request and does not charge a card. The reservation becomes final only after availability, vehicle assignment, route costs, pricing, and written terms are confirmed.
